newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real drops 0.03 pct in seesaw trade.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real drops 0.03 pct in seesaw trade.

text.p: Brazil's real dropped 0.03 percent to close at 1.0830 per dollar in seesaw trade in the commercial foreign exchange market, dealers said.
The local currency traded between 1.0828 and 1.0833 reais per greenback with players taking direction from dollar flows throughout the day, dealers added.

Because the stock of dollars in the market is small this week, expectations of a net dollar outflow put pressure on the real, dealers said. The currency recovered some in late afeternoon, when figures indicated a surplus.
At 1640 local/1940 GMT, preliminary figures for commercial and financial forex contracts showed a $170 million surplus, but some dealers expected that figure to fall by the end of the day.
Dealers also speculated that the real currency was pressured by banks maintaining long positions in the spot market to arbitrage in the dollar futures market on Thursday, the last day of the month.
In the interbank floating rate market, the real closed at 1.0878 per dollar, down 0.01 percent. In the parallel market, the real dropped 0.17 percent to end at 1.152 per dollar.
